prompt_prefix: Return exactly one read-only SQLite SELECT query (WITH is allowed). Return SQL only, without
Markdown. Use the exact target table names.

questionResults.question: How many pantries are in each city?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT 
    a.city, 
    COUNT(p.pantry_id) AS pantry_count
FROM 
    adress a
JOIN 
    pantry p ON a.address_id = p.address_id
GROUP BY 
    a.city;
questionResults.friendlyResponse: Denver has 1 pantry, Phoenix has 1 pantry, and Provo has 1 pantry.

questionResults.question: What is the total quantity of food in each pantry, including shelves and cupboards?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT 
    p.pantry_id, 
    SUM(s.quantity) + SUM(c.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM 
    pantry p
LEFT JOIN 
    shelfs s ON p.pantry_id = s.pantry_id
LEFT JOIN 
    cupboards c ON p.pantry_id = c.pantry_id
GROUP BY 
    p.pantry_id;
questionResults.friendlyResponse: Pantry 1 has a total quantity of 47. Pantry 2 has a total quantity of 22. Pantry 3 has a total quantity of 20.

questionResults.question: Which foods have a quantity of zero, and in which pantry?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT
    p.pantry_id,
    s.food_name
FROM
    pantry p
JOIN
    shelfs s ON p.pantry_id = s.pantry_id
WHERE
    s.quantity = 0

UNION

SELECT
    p.pantry_id,
    c.food_name
FROM
    pantry p
JOIN
    cupboards c ON p.pantry_id = c.pantry_id
WHERE
    c.quantity = 0;
questionResults.friendlyResponse: Canned Soup has a quantity of zero in pantry 3.

questionResults.question: Which pantry has the most food?
questionResults.sql:
WITH food_totals AS (
    SELECT pantry_id, SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity
    FROM (
        SELECT pantry_id, quantity
        FROM shelfs
        UNION ALL
        SELECT pantry_id, quantity
        FROM cupboards
    ) AS combined_food
    GROUP BY pantry_id
)
SELECT pantry_id
FROM food_totals
ORDER BY total_quantity DESC
LIMIT 1;
